source_review.notes: Reviewed current ISO C++ forward_list overview/modifier/operation clauses, Rust recursive-type and Box documentation/source, Linux list and RCU documentation, Clang AddressSanitizer documentation, and Java SE 25 ConcurrentLinkedQueue documentation. All ten final destinations returned HTTP 200.

evidence: Checked abstract sequence, reachability R(head), next, head, tail, size, predecessor, termination, node identity, and half-open sequence notation for consistent use.
Separated node discovery, link rewiring, allocation, destruction, byte/layout, synchronization, and reclamation costs.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Constant-time claims explicitly assume a valid predecessor/cursor and exclude allocation and element callbacks unless stated.

evidence: Replayed append A/B/C, prepend Z, remove B, reverse, temporary cycle injection, and cycle restoration; confirmed final C,A,Z and size 3.
Confirmed the tail terminates after restoration, Floyd observes the injected cycle, and full invariant checking passes afterward.
Recomputed 0+1+...+9999 as 49,995,000 predecessor-link traversals for 10,000 untailored appends.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The trace validates topology and metadata in Python references, not raw-pointer lifetime or general performance.

evidence: Re-derived repeated head-scanning append as n(n-1)/2=Theta(n^2) traversals and tail-based append as O(1) link work per successful append.
Checked access/predecessor/search Theta(n), full traversal/reversal Theta(n), and given-predecessor one-node rewiring O(1).
Checked reversal's processed/unprocessed partition and one-node-decreasing termination measure.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Asymptotic link counts are not promoted to fixed cache, energy, allocator, or latency ratios.

evidence: Reviewed empty, singleton, first/last, erase-after-tail, stored tail/size, sentinel exclusion, maximum size, allocation failure, element-construction failure, and self/overlapping transfer cases.
Reviewed lost suffix, reachable cycle, shared mutable suffix, immutable sharing, recursive destruction depth, stale raw observers, allocator mismatch, slot reuse/generation wrap, and malformed links.
Reviewed concurrent publication, lost update, data races, ABA, memory ordering, delayed reclamation, reader/updater schedules, exhaustion, and safety-sensitive queue boundaries.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The chapter distinguishes managed-reference safety from semantic alias and concurrency correctness.

evidence: Checked head reaches exactly size distinct live nodes, terminates, preserves abstract order, and never exposes a structural sentinel as an element.
Checked empty/nonempty head-tail equivalence, last-node termination, exclusive mutable ownership, and alternative immutable-sharing contract.
Checked insert, erase, reverse, append, clear, transfer, and reclamation metadata obligations.
invariant_checking.notes: Structural sharing is accepted only for an explicitly immutable persistent representation with its own reclamation contract.

evidence: Reviewed construct-before-publish insertion and save-redirect-retire erasure against abstraction and failure guarantees.
Reviewed reversal line by line for suffix preservation, disjoint partition, node-set preservation, and tail update.
Reviewed Floyd discussion for its stable-successor premise and deliberately limited diagnostic conclusion.
proof_review.notes: Concurrent correctness and reclamation require algorithm- and memory-model-specific proofs beyond sequential link transitions.

evidence: Representation, insertion, erasure, reversal, and cost arguments identify their ownership and unit-cost premises.
Cache, allocator, concurrency, security, safety, and deployment statements are conditional evidence obligations rather than universal conclusions.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Legacy machine-specific timings and universal pointer-chasing conclusions were not carried into the chapter.

evidence: The standard-library Python snippet passed exact seven-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under recorded Python 3.14.4.
It emits evidence=finite_link_transition_trace, and all ten cited destinations plus all local links were checked directly.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No raw-pointer implementation, allocator failure, sanitizer target, persistent list, arena, ISO library, kernel RCU path, concurrent queue schedule, benchmark, or safety-sensitive deployment was empirically evaluated.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed abstraction, recursive indirection, termination/sentinel, reachability, prepend, insert/erase transition order, tail/size tradeoffs, reversal, cycles, mutable versus immutable sharing, element ownership, destruction depth, iterators, layout/pools, sorting/splicing, concurrency, testing, and measurement.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed construct-before-publish, suffix retention, unlink-before-reclaim, tail/sentinel metadata, allocator compatibility, iterative clear, stable-node versus stable-position semantics, generation handles, model/fault tests, lifetime counters, memory/race tools, schedule exploration, and workload-equivalent benchmarks.

pedagogical_review.notes: Derives operations from the reachability invariant, uses predecessor-aware APIs, supplies a reproduced topology/cycle trace, corrects legacy universal performance claims while retaining disjoint-ownership and persistent-sharing lessons, counters sixteen misconceptions, and includes ten distinct examples plus five progressive exercises with complete answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, source, mathematical, executable-snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external C++/Rust/Java/Linux/allocator/runtime maintainer, concurrency, security, reliability, safety, clinical, medical, privacy, quality, regulatory, legal, operations, architecture, hardware, accessibility, human-factors, or independent academic review is claimed. The chapter and finite trace prove neither arbitrary raw-pointer correctness, allocation/failure safety, cache performance, stack boundedness, iterator validity outside stated contracts, race freedom, linearizability, memory ordering, ABA prevention, reclamation safety, hard latency, certification, nor deployment fitness.
